clue.text: Mound in burnt remainth revealing Semitic goddess

indicators.note: one thing set in another is placed inside it, so the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: burnt remains are ashes; the clue lisps 'remains' as 'remainth', so the ashes are lisped too
a tor is a rocky hill or mound, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An archaeologist digs into a burnt mound and finds an idol of a Semitic goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: The misspelling 'remainth' is deliberate: it tells you to lisp the synonym as well, so the S of the burnt remains becomes TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashtoreth is the Hebrew Bible's name for Astarte, the Phoenician fertility deity worshipped by Semitic peoples.

clue.text: Sons to select fish basket for small rowing boat

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to cull is to pick out or select from a group

explanation.surface: A father sends his boys to pick a basket for the fish they will catch from their little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed packs in two meanings plus wordplay: the same word is a shallow fish basket and a light rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists scull both as a small light rowing boat and as a shallow basket for carrying fish.

clue.text: Downcast, no good going off for alfresco nosh

indicators.note: something going off departs, so those letters leave the longer word

parts.note: a hanging head is a downcast one
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy because the picnic food has spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' looks like food spoiling but signals removal of NG from the end of HANGING.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangi is a Maori meal cooked in an earth oven outdoors, so it is open-air food.

clue.text: Stage that's divided in theatre (kabuki)

indicators.note: the target is split across a word break, sitting partly in each of the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A Japanese kabuki theatre has a stage split into sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks theatrical but means a leg of a journey; TREK straddles theaTRE and Kabuki.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long journey or one leg of it, as a stage is a section of a journey.

clue.text: One exercising choice, apt to dither about last of ten

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter
dithering is dodging back and forth, so the letters move about uncertainly

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word ten

explanation.surface: Someone faced with a choice tends to waver when the number ten comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: An optant is a person who opts, especially one choosing a nationality, so someone exercising a choice.

clue.text: Vegetarian dish with frills unlimited, including an armadillo!

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so the shortened word wraps the next pieces
without limits means without its boundary letters at either end

parts.note: having frills means being frilled
the indefinite article
tatou is a name for an armadillo, from the Tupi word

explanation.surface: A gimmicky vegetable dish arrives with frills and, absurdly, an armadillo in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With frills' is read as one adjective, and 'unlimited' strips both its ends. Tatou is an old South American name for the armadillo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratatouille is a Provençal stew of courgettes, aubergines, tomatoes and peppers, a meat-free dish.

clue.text: French painter losing head? It often ends in a turn

definitions.text: It often ends in a turn

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Maurice Utrillo painted Montmartre street scenes

explanation.surface: A beheaded French artist, as if his story ends with a sudden twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a plot twist but is musical: a trill commonly finishes with a turn, an ornament of notes around the main one.
explanation.definitionFit: Trillo is the Italian term for a trill, an ornament that in performance usually closes with a turn.

clue.text: Family feature apparent in crook's young offspring?

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A family likeness shows up in a criminal's child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' is a part of the face here. The question mark flags that the definition comes from criminals' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinchin is old thieves' cant for a child, so it is a crook's word for a youngster.

clue.text: Jaunty tune is suitable for couples

indicators.note: jaunty means lively and bouncing, so the letters skip into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bouncy melody is just right for pairs on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples' looks like a noun for dancing pairs but is the verb meaning joins together.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple is to join two things, and unites likewise means joins them together.

clue.text: Black dog suitable for member of high society?

parts.note: jet black; jet is a black mineral
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A black dog is the right pet for a socialite.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'high' is literal too: a jetsetter flies about a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetsetter belongs to the wealthy fashionable set who travel by air to smart resorts.

clue.text: Mark beside the old man in bunk?

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A stain next to where Dad sleeps in the bunk bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed but is the verb: to do a bunk is to run off.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarpa is a variant of scarper, slang for running away, which is what bunking off means.

clue.text: Mass out of the way, I cater for men in mess?

definitions.text: I cater for men in mess?

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
something moved out of the way is removed, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass
the letters to be rearranged once one is removed

explanation.surface: A mess officer clears the way and announces that he feeds the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses the anagram words: 'mess' is both the jumble signal and a dining room, so the whole phrase describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectorian is the official in charge of a refectory, the communal dining hall of a monastery or college.

clue.text: West-country watercourse, river he goes round in

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the outer letters wrap the last word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man strolls around the river in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watercourse' suggests the big German river, but the West Country sense is a drainage ditch on the Somerset Levels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Somerset dialect a rhine is a drainage ditch or channel across the Levels, a local watercourse.

clue.text: Defensive ditch, astute, with fish in?

indicators.note: with something in means holding it inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: cute can mean shrewd or clever
to net is to catch fish

explanation.surface: A clever moat stocked with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunette is a narrow trench cut along the bottom of a dry moat, part of a fortification.

clue.text: Filler? It provides finishing touch to hotel

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something added as the last detail of a hotel's decor.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes at the end of INN. Innit, short for 'isn't it', is British slang used as a conversational filler.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is tagged onto sentences in British speech as a meaningless verbal filler, like a tag question.

clue.text: A covering on skin, formerly one with no accompaniment (9, two words)

parts.note: taken as written
a cap is a covering
pell is an obsolete word for skin or hide
a means one, as in a dozen

explanation.surface: Someone's skin was once covered, and they performed solo.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is performed by voices alone without any instrumental support.

clue.text: Collaborative Scottish church group producing short prayers

definitions.meaning: Action of Churches Together in Scotland, an ecumenical body
an act of contrition or faith is a short formal prayer

explanation.surface: An ecumenical group in Scotland writes brief prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is an acronym; the second is the plural of act in its devotional sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic usage an act is a brief set prayer, such as an act of contrition.

clue.text: Hanger-on exercising legal right in court

indicators.note: in places one item inside the letters of the other

parts.note: CT is an abbreviation for court
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A sycophant asserts their legal rights before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A client was originally a dependant of a patron, a follower who hangs on a powerful person.

clue.text: Senior diplomat from China welcomed by Robert maybe?

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken in, so this goes inside the other piece

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general; Robert is one example of a person with that surname
CH is an abbreviation for China

explanation.surface: A top Chinese diplomat is received by a man called Robert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robert maybe' indicates (Robert) E. Lee, whose middle initial is part of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Elchee is a Turkish and Persian word for an ambassador, a high-ranking envoy.

clue.text: Clerk to tease, made to fill small Italian register

indicators.note: something made to fill a space goes inside it, so this piece sits within the next

parts.note: poco is Italian for little
to rot is to chaff or tease
a list is a register of names

explanation.surface: An office clerk is pressured to fill in a small Italian ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: A protocolist is a registrar or clerk who draws up protocols, the official records of proceedings.

clue.text: Change heading for letter rewritten about the first person

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the pronoun
a text rewritten has its contents reorganised, so these letters change order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone redrafts a letter about themselves and gives it a new heading.
explanation.definitionFit: To retitle is to give something a new title, which is to change its heading.

clue.text: Safeguards as on picture being newly framed

indicators.note: putting something in a new frame recomposes it, so the letters are set in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gallery protects a painting while it is put into a new frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Precautions are measures taken in advance to prevent harm, which is what safeguards are.

clue.text: Ring in NZ trees covered with cracks

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the shape goes inside the plural tree name

parts.note: the rimu is a New Zealand conifer, the red pine
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring of New Zealand trees whose bark is all split.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimous is a botanical term for a surface full of chinks or fissures, such as cracked bark.

clue.text: Melodious Italian poet of yesteryear, not tense inside

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is dropped from the middle of the name
inside says where the dropped letter sits, within the name rather than at an end

parts.note: Ludovico Ariosto wrote Orlando Furioso in the sixteenth century
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An old Italian poet whose verse is musical and relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arioso describes music in a lyrical, song-like style between recitative and aria, so tuneful.

clue.text: Swallow on the spot to discern about summer's start

parts.note: in means present, at home or on the spot

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the verb goes round the single letter

parts.note: to get something is to understand or perceive it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the first letter of summer

explanation.surface: Someone watching for the first swallow of summer on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird arriving in summer, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body, to swallow it down.

clue.text: Aboriginal narcotic? Spicy cake is filled with it

indicators.note: something filled with an item holds it inside

parts.note: a puri is a small deep-fried Indian bread
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spiced cake has been laced with a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Pituri is a shrub whose nicotine-rich leaves Indigenous Australians chew as a stimulant.

clue.text: Like builders at work, unit about to take a rest

indicators.note: going about something and taking it in means enclosing it

parts.note: one is the unit number
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Builders on the job, with a team pausing for a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: Onsite means located at the place of work itself, where builders are while they work.

clue.text: The old shut in pulpit, not initially mobile

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter named is dropped

parts.note: a mimbar is the pulpit in a mosque

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: initially picks the first letter of mobile

explanation.surface: An old cleric trapped in a pulpit, unable to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' does double work: it picks the first letter of mobile and that letter goes from the front of the pulpit word.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbar is an obsolete verb meaning to bar in, to enclose or shut someone up.

clue.text: What Scottish seers use to penetrate extremes of terrible grief as before

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so this goes between the other letters
extremes are the two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of terrible
een is Scots for eyes, which seers see with

explanation.surface: Scottish prophets foresee dreadful sorrow, as in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seers' looks like prophets but just means people who see.
explanation.definitionFit: Teene is an obsolete spelling of teen, an archaic word for sorrow or injury.

clue.text: Ruler recalling wrongdoing, not the first (look in the mirror)

indicators.note: recalling calls something back, so the word runs backwards
the opening letter is left out

parts.note: a crime is a wrongdoing

indicators.note: to look in something is to search inside it, where the answer lies concealed across the words

parts.note: a second, confirming route: the letters run on across these two words

explanation.surface: A ruler remembers a past misdeed and is told to take a hard look at himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a bonus: besides the reversal, the answer sits in plain sight across 'the mirror', which is also an apt image for reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, especially in the Middle East.

clue.text: The best of north England timber part of the kingdom cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Wales is a country of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Fine timber from the north of England, from one area of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings plus wordplay: wale is northern dialect for the pick of something, and a wale is a heavy plank on a ship's side.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect wale means choice or the pick, and wales are thick strakes of a ship's timber.

clue.text: House in favour of abstinence in the toilet

indicators.note: in places one item within the letters of the next

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A household opposed to drink, even in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the bingo call for a full card, and the game is also called lotto.
explanation.definitionFit: House, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo, the game also known as lotto.

clue.text: Late sleeper bailed out around middle of elevenses

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the middle one
out means disordered or wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the middle of a word with an odd number of letters is its central letter

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone who sleeps in walks out midway through the mid-morning tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack break.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is someone who stays in bed late, a late riser.

clue.text: Half sin? More than half — they're humdingers

indicators.note: half keeps only the first two of four letters
more than half keeps three of four letters, dropping just one

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone half-sinful, then rather more, dismisses doubts with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: The same sin is used twice: its first half, then its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is an informal word for an outstanding person or thing, as is a humdinger.

clue.text: Canting character chronicled, first to talk?

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C.S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of talk

explanation.surface: A hypocritical figure in a story is the first to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canting' looks like hypocritical talk but means tilting, and 'chronicled' points to the Narnia books.
explanation.definitionFit: To cant is to tilt, so canting means sloping, which is what aslant means.

clue.text: Edward goes after frisky courtesan lacking sex appeal, frustrated

indicators.note: frisky means playful and lively, so these letters jump about
lacking means without, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, once some are removed
SA is the abbreviation for sex appeal
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward pursues a lively courtesan who has lost her allure, and is thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter a plan is to oppose it, so countered means frustrated or thwarted.
